Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
банка
Wikipedia bg

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈbaŋkɐ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -aŋkɐ
  • Syllabification(key): бан‧ка

Etymology 1

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *bʰeg-der.
Proto-Germanic *bankiz
Proto-West Germanic *banki
Lombardic bankbor.
Italian bancabor.
Ottoman Turkish بانقهbor.
Bulgarian банка

    Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بانقه, borrowed from Italian banca. First attested in 1853.

    Noun

    [edit]

    ба́нка • (bánka) f

    1. (banking) bank (financial institution and the building itself)
    2. (gambling, in the singular) bank (fund or sum of money)
    3. (gambling, in the singular) banker (person running the game)
    4. bank (facility for storing biological products)
      кръ́вна ба́нка
      krǎ́vna bánka
      blood bank
    5. (computing) bank, database

    bánka     		ба́нки
    bánki
    definite ба́нката
    bánkata     		ба́нките
    bánkite

        Borrowed from Russian ба́нка (bánka), borrowed from German Bank.

        Noun

        [edit]

        ба́нка • (bánka) f

        1. (geology) bank, shoal, sandbank (underwater relief form)
        2. (paleontology) bank (accumulation of shells)
        3. school, shoal (group of fish)

        Etymology 4

        [edit]
        Etymology tree
        Old Polish bańka
        Polish bańkabor.
        Bulgarian банка

          Borrowed from Polish bańka.

          Noun

          [edit]

          ба́нка • (bánka) f

          1. flask, bottle, vial (cylindrical glass container used for transfusing bodily fluids)
            ба́нка с глико́за
            bánka s glikóza
            flask / bag of glucose
          2. (countable) The amount of fluid contained in such a vessel.
            Преля́ха ми три ба́нки кръв.
            Preljáha mi tri bánki krǎv.
            They transfused me with three bags of blood.

          Pannonian Rusyn

          [edit]

          Etymology

          [edit]

            Inherited from Old Slovak banka, ultimately from Italian banca. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn банка (banka), Serbo-Croatian банка / banka and Slovak banka.

            Pronunciation

            [edit]
            • IPA(key): [ˈbaŋka]
            • Rhymes: -aŋka
            • Hyphenation: бан‧ка

            Noun

            [edit]

            банка (banka) f (relational adjective банков)

            1. bank (financial institution)

            Russian

            [edit]

            Pronunciation

            [edit]
            • IPA(key): [ˈbankə]
            • Audio:(file)
            • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

            Etymology 1

            [edit]

            Inherited from Proto-Slavic *banъka, from *baňa +‎ *-ъka.

            Noun

            [edit]

            ба́нка • (bánka) f inan (genitive ба́нки, nominative plural ба́нки, genitive plural ба́нок, diminutive ба́ночка)

            1. jar, pot
              • 1905, Фёдор Сологуб [Fyodor Sologub], chapter XIX, in Мелкий бес; English translation from John Cournos and Richard Aldington, transl., The Little Demon, New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 1916:
                И ему́ бы́ло доса́дно, заче́м для Му́рина поста́вили варе́нье, а когда́ он пришёл, то для него́ не хотя́т принести́ но́вой ба́нки с варе́ньем полу́чше.
                I jemú býlo dosádno, začém dlja Múrina postávili varénʹje, a kogdá on prišól, to dlja nevó ne xotját prinestí nóvoj bánki s varénʹjem polúčše.
                And he felt vexed because they put jam before Mourin, and when he came they didn't take the trouble to get a new jar of better jam.
            2. can, tin
            3. (medicine) cupping glass
            4. (in the plural, figuratively, slang) guns (muscles)

            Etymology 2

            [edit]

            Borrowed from German Bank or Dutch bank. Doublet of банк (bank).

            Noun

            [edit]

            ба́нка • (bánka) f inan (genitive ба́нки, nominative plural ба́нки, genitive plural ба́нок)

            1. (marine) sandbank, shoal
            2. (marine) устричная банка oyster bed
            3. (boats) thwart (oarsman’s transverse seat)

              Ukrainian

              [edit]
               банка on Ukrainian Wikipedia

              Pronunciation

              [edit]
              • Audio:(file)

              Etymology 1

              [edit]

              Borrowed from Russian ба́нка (bánka), from Ukrainian ба́нька (bánʹka) or Polish bańka,[1] from Proto-Slavic *banъka.

              Noun

              [edit]

              ба́нка • (bánka) f inan (genitive ба́нки, nominative plural ба́нки or банки́, genitive plural ба́нок or бано́к)

              1. jar (approximately cylindrical container)
              2. can, tin (tin-plate canister, often cylindrical, for preserved foods)
                Synonyms: бляша́нка f (bljašánka), консе́рвна ба́нка f (konsérvna bánka)
              3. (alternative medicine, usually in the plural) cupping glass, cup (for cupping therapy)
                Synonym: меди́чна ба́нка f (medýčna bánka)
